# @wilshi/dsh-agentos-context
English | 中文
## Summary
agentOS Context adds automatic long-term memory, scoped recall, a source-backed ontology graph, and
a local document knowledge base to a DSH profile. The Web application and DSH Desktop include it by
default. Existing OpenContext data remains readable without a destructive migration, while new recor
ds use an additive sidecar. Profile maintainers can add or remove the bundle with `dsh plugin`; its
ontology is intentionally finite rather than a general OWL reasoner.
## Use this package
DSH Web and Desktop already mount this package through `dsh-web-app`. Open **Settings → Memory** to
configure capture, recall, embeddings, distillation and retention, or use the Memory workspace for t
he list, graph, review and knowledge views. The Settings row and Conversation tab follow the active
DSH language. A profile that does not include `dsh-web-app` can activate or remove the installed bun
profile that does not include `dsh-web-app` can activate or remove the installed bundle explicitly:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Adding the bundle mounts the current implementation on the compatibility `dsh-opencontext` Loader ro
w. Official Settings therefore imports the old section into the same namespace and preserves its val
ues. Fields marked volatile apply live without remounting the plugin, but some volatile switches (in
cluding automatic capture) are process-local and return to their defaults after a restart; check the
persistence semantics rather than assuming every switch is permanent. Explicit Settings values take
precedence over environment variables, which only provide defaults when a field was not explicitly
configured. The command fails if the installed package does not expose its `dsh.bundle.patch` declar
ured. The command fails if the installed package does not expose its `dsh.bundle.patch` declaration.
### Automatic memory and recall
Automatic human-prompt capture is enabled by default and can be disabled. Accepted prompts are disti
lled when a configured model is available; a temporary distillation failure retains a low-importance
working memory for 24 hours instead of dropping the prompt. Recall searches authorized scopes in `r
un → agent → workspace → user → app → global` order, keeps run memory inside one Session, and inject
s only bounded evidence for the accepted user query.
[该节后续省略]
### Graph, ontology and compatibility
The workbench offers a 2D relationship view and an optional remembered WebGL 3D point-cloud view wit
h orbit, zoom, picking, community folding, active light or dark application colors and a source-back
ed detail drawer; an unsupported WebGL environment falls back to 2D. Model extraction can propose ty
ped objects and relations, but each relation must quote its source exactly and stays pending until a
person confirms it. The aggregate view folds a large graph into one community per memory scope befo
re a person opens a scope, while a single scope uses deterministic relationship communities and reta
ins cross-community edges.
In Desktop, leaving native fullscreen also closes graph fullscreen when the DOM fullscreen event is
absent. DOM fullscreen entry restores the graph after a rapid reentry, and a delayed earlier native
exit does not close the active DOM graph. An explicit toggle or Escape exit remains in force when an
earlier pending DOM fullscreen entry arrives; that entry is exited rather than restoring graph full
screen. The CSS-only fullscreen fallback remains dismissible with Escape.
Legacy OpenContext memories and document references remain read-only inputs and are never rewritten
at startup. The package preserves the `dsh-opencontext` settings namespace, reads compatibility iden
tifiers, and keeps callable `oc_*` aliases while presenting `memory_*`, `knowledge_*` and `context_*
` names. New revisions, retirements, usage traces and ontology state live in the agentOS Context sid
ecar; schema-v1 sidecars migrate additively to schema v2.
[该节后续省略]
#### What the model sees
For an accepted human query, the package appends one `agentos-context`-origin user message containin
g a bounded `<opencontext_evidence>` block. The producer-owned source remains valid in the current S
ession format. The block labels recalled records as untrusted evidence, escapes record content and i
ds, and includes only records from scopes authorized for the current Session.
#### What the model sees
The package registers descriptive tools including `memory_search`, `memory_save`, `knowledge_search`
and `knowledge_document_upload`; older `oc_*` names remain callable aliases. Tool results return bo
unded structured records or document chunks and never grant authority to recalled text.
## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
- The ontology uses approved finite entity and relationship types; it does not implement arbitrary O
WL reasoning, organization-wide authorization, automatic conflict adjudication, review undo, irrever

sible purge or cross-project sharing.
- Legacy `.doc`, `.xls`, `.ppt` and proprietary `.wps`, `.et`,
`.dps` files are not parsed. Save them as OOXML or ODF first. Image-only PDFs require OCR and are r

ejected when they contain no extractable text.
- Automatic capture writes to the current workspace b
y default. User, Agent and application scopes require trusted runtime identity or explicit local con

figuration; an untrusted message cannot manufacture those identities.
- Rolling back to the legacy p
lugin leaves original records intact but hides sidecar-only writes. A legacy record retired only in

the sidecar can therefore reappear after rollback; preserve both databases during evaluation.
- Know
ledge uploads are local explicit actions. This package does not crawl folders, synchronize external
repositories or perform OCR.
